newsitem.title: FRANCE: EU wheat trickled out in last days of export tax.
newsitem.headline: EU wheat trickled out in last days of export tax.

text.p: European Union wheat export commitments rose 1,000 tonnes in the past week -- even as the EU kept up a wheat tax designed to curb sales ahead of the harvest, official figures showed on Friday.
Total commercial soft wheat export commitments between July 1 last year and June 10 reached 9.789 million tonnes, against 9.788 million by June 3.
The increase appeared to suggest a small quantity of exports leaving at the EU's then prevailing tax of five Ecus per tonne.
The tax was abolished on Thursday.
France said earlier this week that traders had booked licences for some 280 tonnes of wheat at a five Ecu tax, seen likely to cover truckloads from France to Switzerland.
Major world market exports are not commercial, even now that the tax has been abolished, traders say.

Total grain and product export commitments since July have now reached 26.774 million tonnes, up from 26.765 million a week before, while imports have broken through four million tonnes to reach 4.284 million against the previous 3.947 million.
